newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP offer for Cerus this week - paper.
newsitem.headline: CGIP offer for Cerus this week - paper.

text.p: French company CGIP is expected this week to launch a bid for Cerus, the French holding company controlled by Italian industrialist Carlo De Benedetti, the business daily Les Echos said on Tuesday.
It said CGIP would bid between 175 and 180 francs per share for two-thirds of Cerus which would value the company at 7.4 billion francs and assure CGIP control.

In a second stage, Cerus, which controls 28 percent of the capital and 42 percent of the voting rights of Valeo, would offer "an exit" to minority shareholders of the car parts maker, possibly at a price of around 330 francs per share.

Valeo shareholders would have the possibility of receiving two new convertible Cerus bonds for one Valeo share. These would probably be four percent bonds carrying a due date of 2001, the newspaper said quoting sources close to the operation.
The other possibility would be one convertible Cerus bond for one Valeo share, the newspaper said.

Later on, Cerus and Valeo are expected to merge, and electronics group Sagem, which had previously expressed an interest in Valeo, would either join the group through a rights issue that would give it up to 20 percent or link up some of its operations separately with those of Valeo.
